Multi-ordering CAVI

Source: vignettes/cavi_partition.Rmd
cavi_partition.Rmd

This page describes the structured CAVI algorithm for the multiple-ordering model. The tutorial presents the model and software use; this page gives the variational family and the updates used to fit it.

There are n samples, P features, M orderings, and K grid positions. C_i^{(m)} is sample i’s position along ordering m, Z_j is feature j’s ordering assignment, and U_j is its trajectory. Position probabilities are \pi_{mk}, assignment prior weights are \omega_m, noise variances are \sigma_j^2, and smoothness precisions are \lambda_{jm}. The random-walk precision Q_K acts along the grid.

Variational family

MPCurver uses the structured variational family

q(C,Z,U) = \prod_{m=1}^M\prod_{i=1}^n q(C_i^{(m)}) \prod_{j=1}^P q(Z_j)q(U_j\mid Z_j).

Write r_{imk}=q(C_i^{(m)}=k) and w_{jm}=q(Z_j=m), with

q(U_j\mid Z_j=m)=N(\mu_{jm},V_{jm}).

Keeping the trajectory posterior conditional on the feature assignment represents uncertainty about both its shape and its ordering. Each possible assignment has a trajectory mean and covariance, including assignments with small w_{jm}.

The algorithm maximizes the evidence lower bound (ELBO) by alternating trajectory, sample-position, feature-assignment, and parameter updates. Fitting uses temperature T=1 throughout by default, with no annealing.

Conditional trajectories

Let R^{(m)}=(r_{imk}). Define the expected sample count in bin k of ordering m and the corresponding K-dimensional count vector as

n_{mk}=\sum_{i=1}^n r_{imk},\qquad \mathbf n_m=(n_{m1},\ldots,n_{mK})^T.

Each sample contributes its position probability to each bin, so \sum_{k=1}^K n_{mk}=n for every ordering. These are soft sample counts. Conditional on Z_j=m,

A_{jm}=\lambda_{jm}Q_K+ \operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{\mathbf n_m}{\sigma_j^2}\right),\qquad b_{jm}=\frac{(R^{(m)})^T X_{\cdot j}}{\sigma_j^2},

V_{jm}=A_{jm}^{-1},\qquad \mu_{jm}=V_{jm}b_{jm}.

These updates combine the smoothness prior with the full likelihood conditional on that assignment. The conditional trajectory posterior is proper when A_{jm} is positive definite, so its covariance A_{jm}^{-1} exists.

Sample positions

The position update weights each feature by its assignment probability:

\log r_{imk}\stackrel{+}{=} \log\pi_{mk}-\frac12\sum_{j=1}^P w_{jm} \frac{(x_{ij}-\mu_{jmk})^2+V_{jm,kk}}{\sigma_j^2}.

Here \stackrel{+}{=} means equality up to a normalizing constant over k. A feature with large w_{jm} contributes more to ordering m. The posterior variance V_{jm,kk} propagates trajectory uncertainty into the position update.

Feature assignments

For each feature and ordering, the local objective B_{jm} combines expected log likelihood, expected trajectory log prior, and trajectory entropy. Assignment probabilities then satisfy

w_{jm}=\frac{\omega_m\exp(B_{jm})} {\sum_{\ell=1}^M\omega_\ell\exp(B_{j\ell})}.

Thus assignments depend on data fit, smoothness, and posterior uncertainty.

Define the expected residual sum of squares and roughness as

E_{jm}=\sum_{i,k}r_{imk} \left[(x_{ij}-\mu_{jmk})^2+V_{jm,kk}\right],\qquad G_{jm}=\mu_{jm}^TQ_K\mu_{jm}+\operatorname{tr}(Q_KV_{jm}).

Let \rho=\operatorname{rank}(Q_K). These quantities also determine the noise-variance and smoothness updates below.

Local objective for a feature assignment

Writing |Q_K|_+ for the generalized determinant, the standard local objective is

\begin{aligned} B_{jm}=\;&-\frac n2\log(2\pi\sigma_j^2)-\frac{E_{jm}}{2\sigma_j^2}\\ &+\frac12\left[\rho\{\log\lambda_{jm}-\log(2\pi)\} +\log|Q_K|_+-\lambda_{jm}G_{jm}\right]\\ &+\frac12\left[K\log(2\pi e)+\log|V_{jm}|\right]. \end{aligned}

The intrinsic prior uses a fixed reference measure on its null space. An optional smoothness-parameter prior adds \log p(\lambda_{jm}) to this expression; its contribution is zero in the standard model.

Empirical-Bayes parameters and stopping

With E_{jm} and G_{jm} as defined above, the standard parameter updates are

\widehat{\sigma_j^2}=\frac1n\sum_{m=1}^M w_{jm}E_{jm},\qquad \widehat{\lambda}_{jm}=\frac{\rho}{G_{jm}},

\widehat{\pi}_{mk}=\frac1n\sum_i r_{imk},\qquad \widehat{\omega}_m=\frac1P\sum_j w_{jm}.

The implementation applies numerical bounds to noise variances and smoothness precisions. Each joint sweep updates the conditional trajectories, sample positions and \pi, noise variances and smoothness precisions, then feature assignments and \omega. The model dimension M stays fixed.

Fitting stops when the absolute ELBO increment divided by nP is below tol (default 1e-6), subject to a numerical nondecrease check, or when max_iter sweeps have been reached. The default max_iter is 100; tol = 0 disables early stopping.

Known measurement errors

When S is supplied, S_{ij} is the known measurement standard deviation for sample i and feature j. Replace \sigma_j^2 in the likelihood by the known variance S_{ij}^2. The conditional trajectory precision and linear term become

A_{jm}=\lambda_{jm}Q_K+ \operatorname{diag}_k\!\left(\sum_i\frac{r_{imk}}{S_{ij}^2}\right),\qquad b_{jmk}=\sum_i\frac{r_{imk}x_{ij}}{S_{ij}^2}.

For a feature-specific vector S, use S_{ij}=S_j for every sample i. The sample-position update uses these known variances, and the update of \sigma_j^2 is omitted.
